exposure: Maternal age (<25 years, 25-29 years, 30-34 years, 35-39 years, and ≥ 40 years)
cohort: Nulliparous women with non-anomalous, term, singleton pregnancies undergoing labor induction with intact membranes at a tertiary-care academic hospital from January 2015 to April 2017
finding: There was no association between maternal age and labor induction duration for women under 40 years of age, while women 40 years and older had a slight increase in induction duration and a seven-fold increased risk of induction lasting 60 h or longer.
mod_finding: There was no association observed between maternal age and the rate of cesarean delivery.
